heading: Real Estate Investing: Taxing REITs, Funds & Property
tldr: Investing in real estate can be done directly through physical property, or indirectly via REITs or REIT mutual funds.
Capital gains tax rules differ significantly, especially regarding the holding period for long-term gains.
REITs and REIT mutual funds generally qualify for long-term capital gains after 24 months, unlike physical property which requires 36 months.
Income distributions from REITs (interest, rent, dividends) are taxed differently and may attract TDS.
Your final post-tax returns are heavily influenced by these varied tax treatments and TDS rules.
caption:
Thinking about putting your money in real estate? It's not just about buying a flat. You can also invest in special funds (REITs). Here's a little secret: how you invest changes how much tax you pay and how soon. For some real estate investments, you pay less tax sooner! Knowing these small differences can save you a lot.
